Order 
This application, under Section 482 of CrPC, has been filed seeking quashment of FIR in Crime No.25 of 2023 registered at Police Station Gulabganj, District Vidisha for offences under Sections 498A, 294, 323, 506 and 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, as well as consequential proceedings.
2. Applicant No.1 is husband, applicant No.2 is mother-in-law and applicant No. 3 is father-in-law of respondent No.2.

3. According to prosecution case, respondent No.2 lodged an FIR on 28/02/2023 alleging therein that she got married to applicant No. 1 on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10485 13/12/2015 in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals.
She is blessed with a girl child aged about 6 years.

After her marriage, she started living in her matrimonial house situated in Swarnkar Colony,
Vidisha.
After some time of marriage, applicants started scolding her for bringing less dowry and they also used to abuse and assault her on the ground of dowry.

They were insisting that respondent Saurabh Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124919587/
1 No. 2 should bring an amount of Rs.25 lakhs whereas her father had already given sufficient dowry as per his financial capability. When respondent No. 2 informed applicants that her father cannot give Rs. 25 lakhs, then they continued to treat her with mental and physical cruelty by abusing and assaulting her.

sentences.text: Thereafter, she gave birth to a girl child and accordingly applicants were not happy with her and it resulted in escalation in cruelty.
Her mother-in-law used to assault her by a broom and her husband used to dash her head against a wall.
During her second pregnancy, applicants assaulted her in her abdominal region as a result she suffered an abortion.

When this fact was narrated by her to her parents, then applicants threatened that in case if she wants to stay in her matrimonial house, then she will have to stay in accordance with their dictates, otherwise they would burn her.
On account of continuous cruelty, respondent No. 2 was having pain in her waist as well as backache.
When she requested the applicants to get her treated, then on 25/12/2022 she was ousted from her matrimonial house after being assaulted and she was pushed out of the house.
Applicants also refused to give custody of the child.
At the time of ouster, she was not having anything other than what she was wearing.

By using the mobile of a passerby, she informed the incident to her brother who came to Vidisha to take her back and took her to Bansal Hospital,
Bhopal where it was found that respondent No. 2 was having infection in spinal cord and was also suffering from tuberculosis.

After a month of treatment, she NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10485 got some relief.
However, during this period applicants never contacted her.
In order to save her marital life, she was tolerating the cruelty by her husband, mother-in-law and father-in-law.
On multiple occasions, her father had tried to pacify the situation with the mediation of relatives but cruelty never came to an end.
On 12/02/2023 applicants came to her parental home at Pawai and again demanded an amount of Rs.25 lakhs with clear threat that otherwise they would not keep her.
It was also threatened by her mother-in-law that she would remarry her son.
Applicants also threatened to kill her and give divorce.
She felt quite upset and accordingly the FIR was lodged.
4. Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No.2, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that FIR is belated and is barred by time.
It is submitted that even if the entire FIR is read, then it is clear that respondent No. 2 did not disclose any date on which she was treated with cruelty.
It is further submitted that documentary evidence which was collected by police does not support the bald allegations levelled against applicants.
It is further submitted that when the FIR was lodged on 28/02/2023, then why the police got the complainant medically examined on 06/03/2023.
The allegations made against applicants are omnibus and general in nature.
It is further submitted that supplementary statement of respondent No. 2 was recorded on 24/03/2022 in which she did not make any allegation of her ouster.
It is further submitted by counsel for applicant that Mahila Thana Vidisha had no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the FIR.
5. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: 7 . According to the FIR, cruelty by husband and in-laws of respondent No.2 started after some time of marriage.
They used to assault her, abuse her and when she gave birth to a girl child, then it is alleged that the cruelty also escalated.
Respondent No. 2 was assaulted by mother-in-law by broom and her husband used to dash her head against a wall.

It is true that no dates of the incidents have been mentioned to support the aforesaid allegations, but it is equally true that unless and until a person is in the habit of maintaining a diary, she cannot tell with certainty the date when the cruelty was meted out to her.

The FIR was lodged after 8 years of her marriage but one thing is clear that respondent No. 2 was ousted from her matrimonial house on 25/12/2022 and it is the case of respondent No. 2 that at present she is living in her parental home.
It is also the case of respondent No. 2 that even the custody of child was not given to her by applicants.
8. If the entire allegations are read, then it is clear that respondent No. 2 was ousted from her matrimonial house on account of non-fulfilment of demand of dowry.

9. The Supreme Court in the case of Rupali Devi Vs. State of U.P., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384 has held as under:-
"14. "Cruelty" which is the crux of the offence under Section 498-A IPC is defined in Black's Law Dictionary to mean "the intentional and malicious infliction of mental or physical suffering on a living creature, esp. a human; abusive treatment; outrage (abuse, inhuman treatment, indignity)".

entities.text: Rupali Devi Vs. State of U.P., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Cruelty can be both physical or mental cruelty.

The impact on the mental health of the wife by overt acts on the part of the husband or his relatives; the mental stress and trauma of being driven away from the matrimonial home and her helplessness to go back to the same home for fear of being ill-treated are aspects that cannot be ignored while understanding the meaning of the expression NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10485 "cruelty" appearing in Section 498-A of the Penal Code.

The emotional distress or psychological effect on the wife, if not the physical injury, is bound to continue to traumatise the wife even after she leaves the matrimonial home and takes shelter at the parental home.

Even if the acts of physical cruelty committed in the matrimonial house may have ceased and such acts do not occur at the parental home, there can be no doubt that the mental trauma and the psychological distress caused by the acts of the husband including verbal exchanges, if any, that had compelled the wife to leave the matrimonial home and take shelter with her parents would continue to persist at the parental home.

Mental cruelty borne out of physical cruelty or abusive and humiliating verbal exchanges would continue in the parental home even though there may not be any overt act of physical cruelty at such place.
10.

This Court in the case of Amar Singh vs. Smt. Vimla decided on 22.06.2021 in Criminal Revision No.2376/2020 (Gwalior Bench) has held that compelling a married woman to live in her parental home amounts to cruelty.
11. As respondent No.2 was ousted on account of non-fulfilment of demand of dowry, therefore it is clear that the cruelty is continuous in nature.
Therefore.

It is true that respondent No.2 was got medically examined by the police on 06/03/2023 but from the charge-sheet it is clear that respondent No. 2 was admitted in Bansal Hospital, Bhopal on 28/12/2022 for treatment of her spinal cord.

sentences.text: We have gone through the FIR and the criminal complaint.
In the FIR, the appellants have not been named and in the criminal complaint they have been named without attributing any specific role to them.
The relationship of the appellants with the husband of the complainant is distant.

In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662]it was observed (SCC p. 217, para 5):
"5. ... A tendency has, however, developed for roping in all relations of the in-laws of the deceased wives in the matters of dowry deaths which, if not discouraged, is likely to affect the case of the prosecution even against the real culprits.

entities.text: Kans Raj v. State of Punjab (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662]it
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In their overenthusiasm and anxiety to seek conviction for maximum people, the parents of the deceased have been found to be making efforts for involving other relations which ultimately weaken the case of the prosecution even against the real accused as appears to have happened in the instant case."
The Court has, thus, to be careful in summoning distant relatives without there being specific material.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10485

Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations,
unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations.
Mere naming of distant relations is not enough to summon them in the absence of any specific role and material to support such role.

sentences.text: The parameters for quashing proceedings in a criminal complaint are well known.

If there are triable issues, the Court is not expected to go into the veracity of the rival versions but where on the face of it, the criminal proceedings are abuse of Court's process, quashing jurisdiction can be exercised.

Reference may be made to K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar, (2000) 8 SCC 547 : 2001 SCC (Cri) 27, Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate, (1998) 5 SCC 749 : 1998 SCC (Cri) 1400, State of Haryana v. 13. In the present case, the complaint is as follows:
"Sir, it is submitted that I was married on 18-11-2009 with Sidharath Parakh s/o Manak Chand Parakh r/o Sarafa Bazar in front of Radha Krishna Market, Gwalior according to the Hindu rites and customs.
In the marriage my father had given gold and silver ornaments, cash amount and household goods according to his capacity.
After the marriage when I went to my matrimonial home, I was treated nicely by the members of the family.

When on the second occasion I went to my matrimonial home, my husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law started harassing me for not bringing the dowry and started saying that I should bring from my father 25-30 tolas of gold and Rs 2,00,000 in cash and only then they would keep me in the house otherwise not.
On account of this my husband also used to beat me and my father-in-law NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10485 and my mother-in-law used to torture me by giving the taunts.
In this connection I used to tell my father Kundanmal Oswal, my mother Smt Prem Lata Oswal, uncle Ashok Rai Sharma and uncle Ved Prakash Mishra from time to time.
On 2-4-2010 the members of the family of my matrimonial home forcibly sent me to the house of my parents in Ganj Basoda along with my brother Deepak.
They snatched my clothes and ornaments and kept with them.
Since then till today my husband has been harassing me on the telephone and has not come to take me back.
Being compelled, I have been moving this application before you.
Sir, it is prayed that action be taken against husband Sidharath Parakh, my father-in-law Manak Chand Parakh and my mother-in- law Smt Indira Parakh for torturing me on account of demanding dowry.
14. From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out.
There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home.
Even now she continues to be separated from the matrimonial home as she apprehends lack of security and safety and proper environment in the matrimonial home.
The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out.
Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible."

14. Even otherwise in the light of judgments passed by the Supreme Court in the cases of XYZ v.
State of Gujarat reported in (2019) 10 SCC 337, State of Tamil Nadu Vs. S. Martin & Ors. reported in (2018) 5 SCC 718, Ajay Kumar Das v. State of Jharkhand, reported in (2011) 12 SCC 319, Mohd.

sentences.text: 15. So far as the supplementary statement of respondent No.2 is concerned, it was not related to the atrocities meted out to her.
Even otherwise, in the supplementary statement, she has specifically stated that about 5 years back she had suffered miscarriage of pregnancy on account of beating given by the applicants.
In fact, the aforesaid supplementary statement was only given because of the fact that she could not produce any document in respect of the allegation that she had suffered miscarriage.
She has given an explanation that she was taken to hospital by her in-laws and she was in a very bad shape, therefore, she did not have any document in support of her allegation of miscarriage.

By reading the supplementary statement, it cannot be said that it is in respect of cruelty meted out to her by applicants but it is only in respect of non-availability of documents relating to miscarriage.

16. So far as the territorial jurisdiction of Mahila Thana is concerned, it is suffice to mention here that the FIR was lodged at Police Station Mahila Thana NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10485 Vidisha at Serial No.0 and thereafter it was transferred to Police Station Gulabganj, District Vidisha.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: No police station can refuse to register the FIR on the ground of territorial jurisdiction.
The only requirement is that the concerning police station must transfer the FIR to the police station having jurisdiction to investigate.

17. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that the aforesaid allegations are sufficient to prosecute the applicants for the offences alleged against them.
Accordingly, no case is made out warranting interference.
18. Ex consequenti, application fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE (and)
